newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK CENTRAL BANK TO REJECT VSZ REQUEST.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK CENTRAL BANK TO REJECT VSZ REQUEST.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Tuesday said it will reject on technical grounds a request by steel maker VSZ a.s. to increase its holdings in bank IRB a.s. to over 20 percent.

"We will reject the VSZ (issue) on Wednesday," Tibor Kasiak, head of the NBS banking supervision board, told Reuters. "We will not allow VSZ to have over 15 percent (in IRB)...because they put wrong data in the request."
He declined to confirm directly whether the wrong data concerned VSZ's current stake in the bank.
VSZ's holdings in IRB caused a stir when it was recently revealed that it may have exceeded 15 percent, which by law needs central bank approval.
In August, VSZ asked for central bank permission to increase its stake in IRB, the third largest Slovak commercial bank, to over 20 percent.

Shortly after the request was filed, the Central Securities Registry (SCP) published figures showing VSZ already held some 20 percent of IRB, but later retracted the figures without further explanation.
"Technically, I do not know yet whether VSZ has exceeded the limit, but if we find out they have over 15 percent they will have go back to the original situation," Kasiak said.
Kasiak did not say whether the NBS had yet to receive the information from the SCP, but added: "My colleagues who researched the case are already clear on that, and I will sign it tomorrow".
VSZ is a major client of IRB, accounting for an estimated 1.5 percent of the bank's total loan portfolio.
